findings.problem: S02 is British GQ's May 31, 2022 republication. The piece places the MoMA interview days before the season 2 finale aired (February 2022). findings.acceptance_test: The GQ remark is dated "in early 2022" or "in February 2022, days before the season 2 finale" (or "in a profile published in 2022"). The Lowe line says "in the film released in July 2023" or "in 2023." C09 and C28 agree. "Four years after" stays true.

findings.passage: (Who first suggested leaving is hard to tell from the audio.)
findings.problem: A Whisper medium re-run of 33:08-33:33 renders "Should we leave? / Yeah, I'm done. / Thank you so much. / Cause I was, this is too much." The thanks implies the other speaker offered. A 1 fps frame sheet shows Lowe rising first. At about 35:09-35:17, Fike appears to thank Lowe for "letting us get out" and Lowe replies, "Of course, man. I don't want you to stay anywhere that's hard." The article misattributes nothing, but it understates what the record leans toward. That likely sequence (Lowe offers, Fike accepts with thanks) is more faithful and does not weaken the hook.

evidence.passage:
Ask him about it in different years and you get different jails:
- 2022, to GQ: "It really was just a year off to focus on myself."
- 2023, to the Guardian: "It's more of a purgatory... It sucks, dude."
evidence.reason: Nearly every quotation checks out against the cached text or my own Whisper medium re-runs of the three audio sources: Levinson's full framing, the band-aid, the mentor and stability lines, the mother's testimony, the son passage. Each quote is dated and linked at the point of use. Inference is labeled locally ("My read, which the film cannot prove"; "That is a reconciliation, not proof"). The evidence is honest about independence: it is mostly self-report on promotional rounds, plus three journalists, his mother and a filmed exit. Five context slips keep this from a 9: "weed-high" on the wrong tattoo, the GQ republication month, Capone lines joined across six minutes, an inferred fear-of-rejection continuity stated as fact, and two Armchair speaker turns (jail, arousal setting) settled by turn context rather than by ear.

enneagram.passage: Three things keep Seven in front. The first is the kind of danger he went looking for. A counterphobic Six goes at a threat to master it, and the fear is the point. Fike describes his childhood danger as scenery for a story: "another place," "like we'd traveled through time," "Alice in Wonderland."
enneagram.reason: Costly choices fit the Seven motive and are sourced: cocaine on house arrest because he was "trapped all day" and "bored," which cost him a year in jail; mushrooms before the audition; money used "to have the best time you can"; "ride this bitch out until the wheels fall off." The strongest alternative gets a real hearing in his own words: counterphobic Six, "always in another person," the mentor, the manager arrangement, the 2026 security goals. Six fails on a specific, sourced discriminator: danger as wonder, recurring light retellings, pleasure in a clean slate. Nine, Four and Three are each tested. Not higher because the lead is narrow by the article's own account. The discriminator rests on how he tells stories in promotional settings, which the article concedes, and his dated answers about what steadies him lean Six.

originality.passage: The band-aid is the money and the success, and "I'm doing great" is what it let him say. Any successful addict could reach that insight, and a Three would recognize the money covering the wound. What fits the Seven reading is the cheerful cover. The Enneagram word for this is reframing. His word is a Transformers band-aid.
originality.reason: The portrait is built from details only he supplies: the Transformers band-aid, the Forest of Avalon told three ways over six years, three dated jails, the tiles laid under his feet, "Babydoll" whispered in the little sister room on house arrest. The head-triad primer is tied to the motel scene rather than stock type language, and the same-type similarity scan comes back clear. A few rival-type sentences still lean on generic type descriptions ("Fours tend to keep the wound").

writing.passage: "Everyone knows you" in 2018, "no one knows you" in 2025: seven years apart, the same pleasure in a clean slate.
writing.reason: Clean, varied sentences, and each section adds new evidence rather than restating the thesis. Lines like the clean-slate pairing, "He went looking for a story" and the house-arrest ending land without flourish. It runs 4,286 words against a 2,000-3,500 target. The Six case returns across four sections. Repeated hedges ("My read," "My reading," "It cannot prove it") pile up, and some phrasing is clunky ("In his most recent statement on it found as of October 2026, in April 2026, he said"). The pacing in "Why not Type 6?" sags under the weight of sub-arguments.

durability.passage: As of October 2026, the test that would settle it had not been run. The next time something goes badly in public, whether a relapse, a flop or a breakup, listen to how he tells it a year later.

Changing facts are dated and tracked: peak-neutral chart wording, "By October 2026" album count, sobriety answers dated, Euphoria season 3 unresolved with an HBO-credits trigger. The settle signal is concrete and observable with a reopen date. The thesis itself sits close to a flip that the article names.

hook.passage:
Then Lowe asked whether it was weird being back in the room.

> "It's really weird. I feel like tense."

Within seconds both men were on their feet and out the door.
hook.reason: A specific, verified, filmed moment, embedded at the exact timestamp. It sets up the article's real question about leaving, and the band-aid and closing house-arrest irony pay it off. The honest hedges right after ("the beach proves little") cost a little momentum. The exit itself is ambiguous as to who proposed it.

discoverability.passage: meta_title: 'Dominic Fike''s Personality Type: The Case for Enneagram 7'; description: Dominic Fike called jail "a year off," later "a purgatory," and walked out of his childhood motel room on a 2023 visit. Why Type 7 narrowly leads Type 6.
discoverability.reason: The meta title is 57 characters and states the answer. The 153-character description is accurate and signals the margin. The plain type answer runs under 60 words, and the FAQ mirrors it. Six FAQs match real searches ("Babydoll," son, sober, Type 6), all dated and consistent with the body. Internal links go to published Type 6 and Type 7 pages, Dax Shepard and a Type 7 growth post, with five published suggestions. Only four in-body internal links, and the long, clever H1 ("Transformers Band-Aid...Why He Leaves the Room") is less searchable than the meta title.
